01Introduction · Introduction — Embedded AI se parichay

Embedded AI kya hai — edge par intelligence kyun

Embedded AI ka matlab hai — intelligence ko device ke andar hi daal dena. Aam taur par AI ka matlab hota hai bada server, cloud, internet connection aur bahut saari bijli. Embedded AI iska ulta hai: chhota chip, chhoti battery, bina internet ke, aur decision wahi par — device ke andar.

Socho: ek doorbell camera jo aadmi ko pehchan le, ek hearing aid jo shor hata de, ek robot jo girne se pehle khud ko sambhal le — ye sab cloud se poochkar nahi hota. Ye device khud decide karta hai, milliseconds me.

Edge ka matlab: jahan data paida hota hai, wahi par uska faisla ho. Cloud par bhejna matlab hai latency (deri), bandwidth (data kharcha), privacy risk aur internet par nirbharta. Embedded AI in chaaro ko kam karta hai.

Teen badi wajahen — kyun embedded AI ab zaroori hai:

  • Latency: safety-critical kaam — jaise car ka brake ya robot ka balance — cloud ka jawab wait nahi kar sakta. Decision milliseconds me chahiye.
  • Privacy: camera aur microphone ka data ghar se bahar na jaye, to behtar hai. On-device processing me data device par hi rehta hai.
  • Power aur cost: hamesha-on device (jaise wake-word detector) ko microwatt me chalna chahiye, sau watt me nahi. Battery par chalne wala device cloud se baat karke battery khatm nahi kar sakta.

Is book ka vaada: theory ke saath-saath 32 projects hain — har project me asli hardware, asli code aur asli measurements. Tum signal generator se shuru karke, battery monitor, MIDI synthesizer aur hot-word engine tak jaoge.

Ek zaroori sach: embedded AI me machine learning sirf ek tool hai. Asli kaam hai sensing, timing, power aur physics ko samajhna. Jo log sirf model train karte hain, wo device par fail hote hain — kyunki device par data ganda hota hai, sensor drift karta hai aur battery khatm hoti hai.

Book ka roadmap — 14 chapters, 32 projects

Book ko chaar hisso me baanta ja sakta hai. Pehla hissa neenv hai (Ch 1–2): intelligence kya hai, embedded system kya hai, aur pehla project — signal generator.

Dusra hissa machine learning hai (Ch 3–5): ML ki buniyad, deep learning, aur data ko samajhne ke liye EDA. Yahan battery SOC prediction ke projects hain — pehle lookup table se, phir Gaussian Process Regression se.

Teesra hissa sensors aur audio hai (Ch 6–10): smart sensors, IMU preprocessing, sensor fusion, sensor ML aur real-time audio noise suppression. Yahan robot arm fault detection aur Pico par RNNoise jaise projects hain.

Chauthe hisse me poore systems bante hain (Ch 11–13): AI MIDI synthesizer, hot-word detection engine aur battery monitor shields. Epilogue me primal layers framework — dimaag se prerit architecture — aur PrimalBot robot hai.

32 projects, ek list me: Ch 2 me 1 project, Ch 3 me 2, Ch 4 me 3, Ch 5 me 1, Ch 6 me 2, Ch 7 me 1, Ch 8 me 4, Ch 9 me 1, Ch 10 me 2, Ch 11 me 8, Ch 12 me 4, Ch 13 me 3. Har project ka hardware aur platform alag hai — Raspberry Pi Pico, Arduino UNO, Nano 33 BLE Sense, Nicla Vision aur Nicla Voice.

Kaise padhein: chapters kram se padho — har chapter pichle wale par banta hai. Lekin har project apne aap me poora hai: hardware list, circuit, code aur test results sab diye gaye hain.

04Chapter 1 · The Path to Embedded AI

Intelligence aur cognition ka spectrum

Intelligence koi on/off switch nahi hai — ye ek spectrum hai. Book kehta hai ki chetna (consciousness) ki tarah, intelligence bhi halki se gehri hoti hai. Ek thermostat bhi ek tarah se "decide" karta hai, lekin uski intelligence ek bacteria jitni bhi nahi.

Cognition ke components: perception (sense karna), memory (yaad rakhna), learning (seekhna), reasoning (tark karna), planning (yojana banana) aur action (amal karna). Har component alag-alag level par ho sakta hai.

Ek simple embedded device me sirf perception + action hota hai — jaise thermostat: temperature sense karo, heater on/off karo. Ek robot me memory aur learning bhi jud jati hai. Ek LLM me reasoning aur planning bhi hai, lekin uske paas body nahi — isliye wo grounded nahi hai.

Embedded AI ka sawal: in components me se kaunse device par chahiye, aur kaunse cloud par chhod sakte ho? Jo component milliseconds me chahiye (jaise reflex), wo device par hona chahiye. Jo ghanton me bhi chalega (jaise lambi planning), wo cloud par ho sakta hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: intelligence ka matlab sirf "bada model" nahi hai. Ek chhota model jo sahi jagah, sahi waqt par, sahi decision le — wo zyada intelligent system hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 1 — The Path to Embedded AI

05Chapter 1 · The Path to Embedded AI

AI ka evolutionary tree

AI ek hi raat me nahi bana. Book AI ke vikas ko ek evolutionary tree ki tarah dikhata hai — har shakha pichli shakha ki kami ko door karti hai.

  • 1950s — Symbolic AI: rules aur logic se reasoning. Chess jaise band (closed) problems me accha, lekin real duniya ki gandagi (noise, uncertainty) me fail.
  • 1958 — Perceptron: pehla neural network. Sirf linear problems solve kar sakta tha — XOR bhi nahi. Isi kami ne pehla "AI winter" laaya.
  • 1980s — Expert systems: human experts ke rules ko code me daalna. Kaam kiya, lekin rules likhna mehenga aur brittle tha.
  • 1990s–2000s — Machine learning: rules likhne ki jagah data se seekhna. Support vector machines, decision trees, random forests.
  • 2012 ke baad — Deep learning: bade data + GPUs ne deep networks ko practical banaya. Image aur speech me kranti.
  • 2017 ke baad — Transformers aur LLMs: attention mechanism ne language models ko scale kiya. Aaj ke LLMs isi shakha ke phal hain.
  • Ab — Embedded AI: in models ko chhota, tez aur sasta karke device par le jana. Quantization, pruning, TinyML aur neuromorphic chips isi shakha hain.

Embedded engineer ke liye lesson: har generation ki taakat aur kamzori samajhna. Deep learning pattern recognition me best hai, lekin reasoning aur grounding me kamzor — isliye embedded system me use classical techniques (Kalman filter, FSM, PID) ke saath jodna padta hai.

06Chapter 1 · The Path to Embedded AI

AGI model aur OpenAI ke 5 levels

Book ek conceptual AGI model deta hai — artificial general intelligence ko ek hi model ki tarah nahi, balki layers ki tarah dekhna chahiye. Neeche reflex aur control hain, upar reasoning aur planning.

OpenAI ke 5 levels (Table 1-1):

LevelNaamMatlab
1ChatbotsConversation kar sakne wala AI — aaj ke LLMs yahin hain
2ReasonersDoctorate-level problem solving — maths, science, code me expert reasoning
3AgentsKhud action lene wala AI — tools use karke kaam poora kare
4InnovatorsNayi cheezein invent karne wala AI — research aur discovery
5OrganizationsPoori organization ka kaam karne wala AI — sabse upar ka level

Embedded AI ka angle: Levels 1–2 aaj cloud par hain. Level 3 (agents) ko device par laana hi embedded AI ka kaam hai — kyunki agent ko duniya me action lena hai, aur action ke liye body, sensors aur real-time response chahiye.

Sachai check: aaj ke LLMs Level 1 par mazboot hain, Level 2 ki taraf badh rahe hain. Level 3–5 abhi roadmap hain, reality nahi. Book ka primal layers framework kehta hai ki in levels tak pahunchne ke liye sirf neocortex ko bada karna kaafi nahi — neeche ki layers (reflex, motivation, skill) bhi chahiye.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 1 — The Path to Embedded AI

07Chapter 1 · The Path to Embedded AI

Embedded vs cloud vs edge vs AIoT

Book chaar architectures ko block diagrams se samjhata hai. Har ek me data kahan process hota hai, ye alag hai.

Embedded AI: sab kuch device par. Sensor → microcontroller → decision → actuator. Koi network nahi, koi der nahi. Example: Nicla Voice par hot-word detection — <1 mW me hamesha sunta rehta hai.

Cloud-based AI: device sirf data bhejta hai, decision cloud par hota hai. Taakat zyada, lekin latency, bandwidth aur privacy ki keemat. Example: voice assistant jo har command cloud bhejta hai.

Edge computing: beech ka rasta — device ke paas ek local gateway/server (jaise Raspberry Pi ya local server) decision leta hai. Cloud se kam latency, device se zyada taakat.

AIoT (AI + IoT): cloud-based AIoT me devices, gateway aur cloud teeno judte hain. Device data collect karta hai, gateway filter karta hai, cloud deep analysis karta hai.

Kaunsa kab chunna hai — decision table:

ZarooratSahi architecture
Milliseconds me response, safety-criticalEmbedded AI
Bada model, heavy compute, der chalegiCloud AI
Kai devices, local coordination, moderate latencyEdge computing
Poori fleet ka data, trends, long-term analysisAIoT (cloud + edge)

Asli systems hybrid hote hain: hot-word device par detect hota hai, baaki baatchit cloud par hoti hai. Yehi pattern Ch 12 me dikhega.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 1 — The Path to Embedded AI

08Chapter 1 · The Path to Embedded AI

Energy efficiency — 20 watt dimag vs sau watt LLM

Human brain lagbhag 20 watt par chalta hai — ek halke bulb jitni bijli. Isi 20 watt me wo dekhna, sunna, chalna, bolna aur sochna — sab kuch karta hai. Ek frontier LLM ko chalane me prati user session sau watt se zyada lag sakte hain, aur train karne me gigawatt-hours.

Energy efficiency vs performance ka graph (Figure 1-8): jaise-jaise performance badhta hai, energy kharcha tezi se badhta hai. Diminishing returns — aakhri 1% accuracy ke liye 10x energy lag sakti hai. Embedded engineer ka kaam hai is curve par sahi point chunna.

91% ka ankda: ek model drift study kehta hai ki 91% ML models samay ke saath degrade hote hain — data badalta hai, sensor badalta hai, duniya badalti hai. Isliye embedded ML me sirf train karna kaafi nahi; monitor karna aur retrain karna bhi system ka hissa hai.

Embedded AI me energy bachane ke 5 tareeke:

  • Quantization: float32 ki jagah int8 — model ~4x chhota, inference tez. (Ch 11 me poora project hai.)
  • Pruning: bekar weights hata do — model chhota, accuracy lagbhag wahi.
  • Efficient architectures: MobileNets jaise halke networks — Ch 4 me person detection me istemal hote hain.
  • Hardware accelerators: NDP120 jaise neural processors — <1 mW me hamesha-on inference.
  • Event-driven compute: sirf tab compute karo jab kuch badle — neuromorphic approach, Epilogue me.

Interview me poocha jata hai: "Model ko device par chalane ke liye sabse pehle kya karoge?" Jawab: pehle measure karo — model ka size, latency aur power — phir quantization aur pruning se sahi trade-off chuno.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 1 — The Path to Embedded AI

09Chapter 2 · The Basics of Embedded Systems

Embedded system kya hai — characteristics

Embedded system wo computer hai jo dikhta nahi. Tumhare car me 100 se zyada embedded systems hain — engine control, brakes, airbags, infotainment. Tumhe pata bhi nahi chalta, kyunki wo ek hi kaam karte hain, aur use hamesha karte hain.

Embedded systems ki 7 pehchan:

  • Dedicated function: ek hi kaam, lekin wo kaam perfect. General-purpose computer ki tarah har kaam nahi.
  • Real-time constraints: jawab sahi waqt par aana chahiye — der se aaya sahi jawab bhi galat hai.
  • Resource-constrained: KBs me memory, MHz me speed, mW me power. Har byte ki keemat hai.
  • Reliability: saalon tak bina restart ke chalna chahiye. Koi "reboot karke dekho" nahi.
  • Interaction with physical world: sensors se input, actuators se output. Physics se seedha samna.
  • Cost-sensitive: lakhon units bante hain — ek dollar bhi badi baat hai.
  • Long lifecycle: device 10–20 saal chal sakta hai; software update mushkil ya namumkin.

Example — car ka embedded system: engine control unit (ECU) har second hazaaron baar sensor padhta hai — temperature, pressure, RPM — aur fuel injection ko microseconds me adjust karta hai. Yehi real-time embedded hai.

Embedded AI isme kya jodta hai: pehle ye systems fixed rules par chalte the. Ab wo data se seekhkar adapt kar sakte hain — jaise battery ka SOC estimate karna ya driver ka behavior samajhna.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 2 — The Basics of Embedded Systems

10Chapter 2 · The Basics of Embedded Systems

Jab embedded fail hota hai — Toyota, Air Inter, Ariane 5

Embedded systems me galti ki keemat jaan ho sakti hai. Book teen mashhoor failures se shuru karta hai — taaki tum samjho ki testing aur safety kyun sabse upar hai.

Toyota unintended acceleration (2009–2011): cars achanak tez ho jati thi. Investigation me software aur safety process dono par sawal uthe. Lesson: safety-critical code me har line ka hisaab hona chahiye, aur fail-safe (kuch gadbad ho to safe state me jao) zaroori hai.

Air Inter Flight 148 (20 January 1992): autopilot me descent rate galat set hua — 3.3° descent angle ki jagah 3,300 feet/minute descent rate select ho gaya. Do alag units, ek hi display — pilot confuse hua, plane pahad se takra gaya. Lesson: UI me mode confusion jaanleva ho sakta hai; units hamesha saaf dikho.

Ariane 5 (4 June 1996): pehli flight ke 37 second me rocket phat gaya — $370 million ka nuksan. Wajah: ek 64-bit float ko 16-bit integer me convert karte waqt overflow ho gaya. Ye code Ariane 4 se liya gaya tha, jahan wo value kabhi itni badi nahi hoti thi. Lesson: reused code ko naye system me bina test ke mat chalao; har conversion ka range check karo.

Teeno se ek hi lesson: embedded me "kaam kar gaya" kaafi nahi hai. Tumhe ye bhi batana hoga ki fail hone par kya hoga — aur fail hone ka tareeka safe hona chahiye. Isi liye book me har project me testing aur measurement par itna zor hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 2 — The Basics of Embedded Systems

11Chapter 2 · The Basics of Embedded Systems

RP2040 memory layout — stack, heap, scratch

Raspberry Pi Pico ka RP2040 chip embedded memory ka best example hai. Isme 264 KB SRAM aur 2 MB flash hai — tumhare phone se lakh guna kam. Phir bhi is par signal generator, audio processing aur ML chal sakta hai.

Memory map (Figure 2-2 ke hisaab se):

  • Flash (2 MB): program code aur constant data yahan rehta hai. XIP (execute in place) se code seedha flash se chalta hai.
  • SRAM (264 KB): 6 banks me bata hua hai. Stack, heap aur data yahin hain.
  • Stack — 2 × 2 KB: har core ke liye alag stack. Function calls aur local variables yahan jate hain. Stack overflow embedded ka classic bug hai.
  • Scratch banks — 4 KB: chhote, tez scratchpad memory. Critical data yahan rakho.
  • Heap: dynamic allocation (malloc) ke liye. Embedded me heap se bacho — fragmentation se system dheere-dheere mar jata hai.

Do golden rules:

  • Static allocation prefer karo: arrays ko compile time par size do. malloc se bacho, khaas taur par loop me.
  • Stack ka size jano: bade arrays ko function ke andar local mat banao — wo stack kha jayenge. Global ya static banao.

Pico block diagram: dual-core Cortex-M0+ (133 MHz), 2 PIO blocks, DMA, ADC, PWM, I2C/SPI/UART. PIO iski superpower hai — Project #1 me tum PIO se signal generate karoge.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 2 — The Basics of Embedded Systems

12Chapter 2 · The Basics of Embedded Systems

Bare-metal vs framework vs RTOS

Embedded software likhne ke teen tareeke hain. Book inki tulna ek table (Table 2-1) me karta hai.

ApproachKya haiKab bestKami
Bare-metal (super loop)Ek loop: read → process → write, baar-baarSimple kaam, ek hi task, deterministic timingComplex kaam me ulajh jata hai
Framework (Arduino)setup() + loop(), libraries readyPrototyping, learning, medium complexityControl kam, overhead zyada
RTOSTasks, priorities, scheduler, queuesKai tasks, strict timing, complex systemsSeekhne me mushkil, debug karna kathin

Super loop ka pattern:

while (1) {
  read_sensors();   // sensor padho
  process();        // decide karo
  write_outputs();  // actuator chalao
}

Interrupt vs polling: polling me loop baar-baar check karta hai — simple lekin CPU waste. Interrupt me hardware batata hai jab kaam ho — efficient lekin likhna mushkil. Project #1 me DMA + interrupt ka combo istemal hota hai.

Is book ka approach: zyadatar projects Arduino framework par hain (seekhna aasan), lekin jahan timing critical hai (Project #1, #17), wahan bare-metal/PIO/DMA istemal hota hai. RTOS is book me nahi — ye agle level ki cheez hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 2 — The Basics of Embedded Systems
← Previous11 · RP2040 memory layout — stack, heap, scratch→ Next13 · Project #1 — Signal Generator (Pico)
13Chapter 2 · The Basics of Embedded Systems

Project #1 — Signal Generator (Pico)

Project #1 me tum Raspberry Pi Pico se ek signal generator banate ho — aisa device jo sine wave jaisi signals paida karta hai. Ye book ka pehla hardware project hai, aur isme PIO, DMA aur DAC — teeno core concepts aa jate hain.

Wavetable synthesis: sine wave ko pehle se calculate karke ek table me store karo — 256 samples, 8-bit (har sample 0–255). Phir table ko baar-baar chalao, to wave ban jati hai. Table jitni badi, wave utni smooth.

PIO (Programmable I/O): Pico ki superpower. PIO ek chhota processor hai jo CPU ko pareshan kiye bina pins ko control karta hai. Signal generator ka PIO program sirf 2 instructions ka hai:

pull   ; FIFO se sample lo
out pins, 8  ; 8 bits ko pins par bhejo

DMA chaining: CPU ko table se PIO tak data bhejne ki zaroorat nahi — DMA (Direct Memory Access) khud data transfer karta hai. Do DMA channels chain karke ek dusre ko trigger karte hain, to signal kabhi nahi rukta.

DAC — R-2R ladder: digital samples ko analog voltage me badalne ke liye R-2R resistor ladder banta hai. Formula:

Vout = (Digital value / 2^N) × Vref — 8-bit ke liye Digital 0–255, Vref 3.3 V.

MCP6001 op-amp buffer: R-2R ladder ki output ko seedha load se mat jodo — op-amp voltage follower lagao, warna load ladder ko bigaad dega.

Frequency ke numbers: interrupt-based approach me ISR lagbhag 38 cycles = 304 ns leta hai, to max frequency lagbhag 206 kHz (interrupt) aur PIO+DMA se 488.28 kHz (256 samples, 125 MHz clock). Table 2-7 ke hisaab se: 128 samples → 977 kHz, 64 → ~2 MHz, 32 → ~3.9 MHz, 16 → ~7.8 MHz. Sample kam karo, frequency badhao — lekin wave kharab hoti jati hai.

Slew rate ki problem: 488 kHz, Vpeak 0.45 V par chahiye 1.38 V/µs, lekin MCP6001 sirf 0.6 V/µs deta hai. Matlab op-amp wave ko follow nahi kar payega — isliye practical frequency isse kam rehti hai. Yehi embedded reality hai: datasheet padho, phir measure karo.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 2 — The Basics of Embedded Systems
← Previous12 · Bare-metal vs framework vs RTOS→ Next14 · ML vs statistics — farak kya hai
14Chapter 3 · Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects

ML vs statistics — farak kya hai

Machine learning aur statistics ek hi ped ki do shakhaen hain — dono data se seekhte hain. Lekin unka focus alag hai. Book Table 3-1 me tulna karta hai.

AspectStatisticsMachine Learning
GoalSamajhna — kyun hua, kaise huaPredict karna — aage kya hoga
ModelSimple, interpretable (linear regression)Complex bhi chalega (neural networks)
DataChhota dataset, assumptions clearBada dataset, assumptions kam
SuccessStatistical significance (p-value)Prediction accuracy (test set par)

Embedded engineer ke liye matlab: device par tumhe prediction chahiye (ML), lekin debugging ke liye samajh bhi chahiye (statistics). Isliye dono ka mix istemal hota hai — jaise Ch 5 me EDA statistics se data samajhna, phir ML se predict karna.

Ek example: battery SOC predict karna. Statistics kahega — voltage aur SOC ka correlation 0.93 hai, linear model banao. ML kahega — Gaussian Process Regression se 0.9961 R² milega. Dono sahi hain; farak sirf itna hai ki tumhe kitni accuracy chahiye aur kitni samajh.

Overfitting ka khatra: ML model training data ko rat sakta hai — test data par fail. Isse bachne ke liye train/validation/test split aur cross-validation zaroori hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 3 — Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects
← Previous13 · Project #1 — Signal Generator (Pico)→ Next15 · ML process — data se deployment tak
15Chapter 3 · Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects

ML process — data se deployment tak

ML project koi ek step nahi — ye ek pipeline hai. Book kehta hai ki 80% kaam data par hota hai, 20% model par. Jo ye ulta karte hain, wo fail hote hain.

ML process ke steps:

  • 1. Problem define karo: kya predict karna hai? SOC? Proximity? Hot word? Metric kya hai — accuracy, RMSE ya F1?
  • 2. Data collect karo: sensor se, public dataset se, ya synthetic. Data ki quality hi model ki quality hai.
  • 3. Data explore karo (EDA): distributions, correlations, outliers, missing values. Ch 5 poora isi par hai.
  • 4. Features banao: raw data se useful signals nikalo — jaise FFT se frequency bands, ya rolling average.
  • 5. Model chuno aur train karo: simple se shuru karo (linear regression), phir complex (GPR, neural network).
  • 6. Evaluate karo: test set par metric dekho. Train accuracy se khush mat ho — test accuracy dekho.
  • 7. Deploy karo: model ko device par chalao — quantization, TensorFlow Lite Micro. Ch 4 aur Ch 11 me yehi hota hai.
  • 8. Monitor karo: model drift hota hai (91% models degrade hote hain) — monitor karo, retrain karo.

Embedded twist: steps 7–8 desktop ML me nahi hote. Device par model ka size, latency aur power — teeno constraints hain. Isliye embedded ML me model chunne se pehle device ki limits janni zaroori hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 3 — Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects
← Previous14 · ML vs statistics — farak kya hai→ Next16 · Linear regression aur normal equation
16Chapter 3 · Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects

Linear regression aur normal equation

Linear regression ML ka sabse simple model hai — aur embedded me sabse useful, kyunki ye chhota, tez aur samajhne layak hai.

Model: y = mx + c. Book ka example: y = 1.05x + 1.35 — slope 1.05, intercept 1.35. Matlab x badhe to y lagbhag utna hi badhe.

MSE (Mean Squared Error): prediction aur actual ke beech ke farak ka square, average. Model jitna accha, MSE utna kam. Book ke example me model ka MSE 1.094 hai.

Normal equation — bina iteration ke solution:

β = (XᵀX)⁻¹ Xᵀy

Ye formula ek hi step me best-fit line nikal deta hai — gradient descent ki tarah hazaar iteration nahi chahiye. Chhote dataset par ye best hai; bade dataset par matrix invert karna mehenga padta hai.

Table 3-2 — actual vs model:

ParameterActualModel
Intercept1.352.196
Slope1.050.909
MSE1.2871.094

Lesson: model ke parameters actual se alag hain, phir bhi MSE kam hai. Matlab model data ko fit karta hai, lekin "sach" ko capture nahi karta. Embedded me ye farak samajhna zaroori hai — tumhe prediction chahiye ya sachai?

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 3 — Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects
← Previous15 · ML process — data se deployment tak→ Next17 · Project #2 — Lookup table se battery SOC
17Chapter 3 · Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects

Project #2 — Lookup table se battery SOC

Project #2 me tum Arduino UNO R3 se ek 3S LiPo battery ka State of Charge (SOC) estimate karte ho — bina kisi ML ke, sirf lookup table se. Ye ML se pehle ka tareeka hai, aur embedded me aaj bhi bahut istemal hota hai.

Problem: battery ka voltage uske SOC ko batata hai, lekin relation linear nahi hai. 3S LiPo ka nominal voltage 11.1 V hai, max 12.6 V. Voltage se SOC nikalne ke liye table chahiye.

Hardware: UNO R3 ka 10-bit ADC (0–1023). Battery voltage ko voltage divider se kam karo: R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 ≈ 6.2 kΩ. ADC ka input impedance dhyan me rakho — charge time 5τ = 7.7 µs, aur max R1 71 kΩ se zyada nahi hona chahiye, warna ADC sahi se charge nahi hoga.

Battery specs: 3S LiPo, 2200 mAh, 25C/35C — peak current 77 A. 15% tak discharge hone me 87.4 second lagte hain; safe limit 122.4 second.

Lookup table: 21 entries — voltage se SOC. ADC reading lo, voltage nikalo, table me nearest entry dhoondho, SOC interpolate karo. Poora kaam microseconds me, bina kisi heavy compute ke.

Limitations: voltage sirf SOC ka rough estimate deta hai — temperature, age aur load se voltage badalta hai. Isi liye Project #3 me ML aata hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 3 — Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects
← Previous16 · Linear regression aur normal equation→ Next18 · Project #3 — GPR se battery SOC (R² 0.9961)
18Chapter 3 · Applied Machine Learning in Embedded Projects

Project #3 — GPR se battery SOC (R² 0.9961)

Project #3 me wahi SOC problem ML se solve hoti hai — Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) se. Dataset hai LG 18650HG2 cell ka public dataset: 669,956 training columns, chaar temperatures par — –10°C, 0°C, 10°C, 25°C.

GPR kya hai: ek probabilistic regression jo sirf prediction nahi deta, balki uncertainty bhi batata hai — "SOC 62% hai, ±3% confidence." Safety-critical kaam me ye uncertainty bahut keemti hai.

Kernel: GPR ka dil. Book me kernel hai C(0.01,(0.001,0.1)) * RBF(0.5,(0.01,1.0)) — constant × radial basis function. GridSearchCV 5-fold cross-validation se best kernel dhoondha gaya.

Trials — kitna time laga:

TrialResult (R²)Time
Trial 1–1102.22 (bilkul fail)15 min 33 sec
Trial 2–1.7544 min 47 sec
Trial 5 (exponential kernel)–0.63—
Trial 60.9808277 min 43 sec

Test results (Table 3-8):

TemperatureR²RMSE
–10°C0.99610.0182
0°C0.99450.0204
10°C0.98830.0291
25°C0.98520.0300

GPR vs lookup table (Table 3-9, –10°C): RMSE 0.0182 vs 0.1031 (82% kam), MAE 0.0083 vs 0.0750 (89% kam), R² 0.9961 vs 0.88. ML jeetta hai — lekin keemat hai: training me ghante, aur device par chalana mushkil. Isliye GPR ko deploy karne se pehle socho: kya lookup table kaafi hai?

19Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

Perceptron se MLP aur XOR tak

Perceptron 1958 me bana — pehla neural network. Ek perceptron inputs ko weights se multiply karke sum karta hai, phir threshold se decide karta hai: 0 ya 1. Simple, lekin sirf linear problems solve kar sakta hai.

XOR problem: XOR (exclusive OR) ko ek perceptron solve nahi kar sakta, kyunki XOR linearly separable nahi hai. Yehi kami 1969 ki kitab ne dikhayi, aur AI winter laayi.

MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) — solution: ek hidden layer jodo, to XOR solve ho jata hai. Hidden layer data ko aisi space me transform karta hai jahan wo linearly separable ho jaye. Yehi deep learning ki buniyad hai: layers data ko aise transform karte hain ki problem aasan ho jaye.

Activation functions:

  • Sigmoid: output 0–1, binary classification ke liye. Lekin gradient vanish karta hai.
  • ReLU: negative ko 0, positive ko waisa hi. Tez, simple, aaj standard hai.
  • Tanh: output –1 se 1, zero-centered.
  • Softmax: multi-class — probabilities ka sum 1 hota hai.

Training — backpropagation: error ko peeche se aage bhejkar weights update karo. Gradient descent se weights dheere-dheere behtar hote hain. Learning rate zyada ho to overshoot, kam ho to slow.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous18 · Project #3 — GPR se battery SOC (R² 0.9961)→ Next20 · Embedded deep learning aur TensorFlow
20Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

Embedded deep learning aur TensorFlow

Deep learning ko device par chalana alag khel hai. Desktop par model GBs ka ho sakta hai; device par KBs ka hona chahiye.

Embedded DL process:

  • 1. Train bada model: desktop/cloud par TensorFlow se train karo — data aur compute dono wahan hain.
  • 2. Optimize karo: quantization (float32 → int8, ~4x chhota), pruning (bekar weights hatao).
  • 3. Convert karo: TensorFlow Lite Micro format me convert karo — microcontroller ke liye.
  • 4. Deploy karo: model ko C array banakar firmware me daalo (xxd -i se). Tensor arena allocate karo.
  • 5. Test karo device par: accuracy desktop jaisi hai ya nahi? Latency kitni hai?

TensorFlow ecosystem: TensorFlow (training), TensorFlow Lite (mobile/edge), TensorFlow Lite Micro (microcontrollers — sirf KBs memory). TFLM me sirf zaroori ops hote hain — har op ko include karne se binary badi hoti hai.

Tensor arena: model ke intermediate tensors ke liye memory. Book ke GAN project me arena sirf 4 KB tha, estimated 3,340 bytes — har byte ginna padta hai.

OpResolver: sirf wahi ops register karo jo model use karta hai. Har extra op flash khata hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous19 · Perceptron se MLP aur XOR tak→ Next21 · Project #4 — ANN se proximity detection
21Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

Project #4 — ANN se proximity detection

Project #4 me tum Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev 2 se proximity detect karte ho — ek chhota ANN (Artificial Neural Network) use karke. Sawal: kya phone kaan ke paas hai ya nahi?

Hardware: Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev 2 — onboard APDS-9960 proximity sensor aur BMI270 IMU. Dono sensors ka data ANN ko milta hai.

Features (4): proximity value, aur IMU se 3 values. Model in 4 inputs se decide karta hai: near ya far.

Architecture: Dense(8, ReLU) + Dense(1, sigmoid). Matlab: input layer (4) → hidden layer (8 neurons, ReLU) → output (1 neuron, sigmoid — 0 se 1 ke beech probability).

Training: 20 Hz sampling rate, 60/20/20 split (train/validation/test). Threshold: >60% = near-ear (kaan ke paas).

Deploy: model ko TFLite Micro me convert karke Nano par chalao. Tensor arena me alignment ka dhyan rakho — alignas(16) se data 16-byte boundary par align hota hai, jo ARM ke liye zaroori hai.

Lesson: chhota model bhi kaam karta hai — 8 neurons ka hidden layer hi kaafi tha. Embedded me hamesha sabse chhota model dhoondho jo kaam kare.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous20 · Embedded deep learning aur TensorFlow→ Next22 · Project #5 — CNN se person detection (Nicla Vision)
22Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

Project #5 — CNN se person detection (Nicla Vision)

Project #5 me tum Arduino Nicla Vision se person detection karte ho — ek CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) jo camera image me aadmi ko pehchanta hai.

Hardware: Nicla Vision — STM32H747 dual-core (M7 480 MHz / M4 240 MHz), GC2145 2MP camera. Itni taakat isliye chahiye kyunki image processing heavy hai.

Model: MobileNets-based person detection, lagbhag 300 KB. Input: 96×96 grayscale image. MobileNets depthwise separable convolution use karta hai — normal convolution se bahut kam compute.

Image pipeline: camera se QQVGA 160×120 RGB565 frame aata hai — 38,400 bytes. Use grayscale me convert karo:

Y = 0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B

Phir 96×96 par resize karo aur model ko do.

TFLite Micro library patches: Nicla Vision par TFLM chalane ke liye 4 library files patch karni padti hain — ye book me step-by-step diya hai. Yehi embedded reality hai: kabhi-kabhi library ko haath se fix karna padta hai.

Example output: person score 77.34% vs no-person 22.65% — model ko lagta hai frame me aadmi hai.

Visual Wake Words dataset: training data COCO dataset se bana hai — person hai ya nahi, ye binary label. Dataset ka naam yaad rakho — interview me poochte hain.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous21 · Project #4 — ANN se proximity detection→ Next23 · RNN, LSTM aur BRNN — sequence models
23Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

RNN, LSTM aur BRNN — sequence models

CNN image ke liye accha hai, lekin time-series data (audio, sensor stream, text) ke liye sequence models chahiye. Book RNN, LSTM aur BRNN ko samjhata hai.

RNN (Recurrent Neural Network): har step par previous output ko input ki tarah use karta hai — memory hoti hai. Lekin lambi sequence me gradient vanish ho jata hai — RNN bhool jata hai.

LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory): RNN ka improved version — gates (forget, input, output) se decide karta hai kya yaad rakhna hai, kya bhoolna hai. Lambi dependencies handle karta hai.

BRNN (Bidirectional RNN): sequence ko aage aur peeche — dono taraf se padhta hai. Jab future context bhi chahiye (jaise poora sentence samajhne ke liye), BRNN best hai.

Kahan istemal hote hain (is book me):

  • GAN music generation (Project #6): discriminator me LSTM + BiLSTM — music sequence ko samajhne ke liye.
  • RNNoise (Ch 10): GRU (LSTM ka halka version) — audio frames ko sequence me process karne ke liye.
  • Hot word detection (Ch 12): CNN zyada istemal hota hai, kyunki spectrogram ko image ki tarah treat kiya jata hai.

Embedded me problem: RNN/LSTM me state maintain karna padta hai — har step par hidden state store karo. Memory aur compute dono zyada. Isliye embedded me GRU ya chhote LSTM prefer karte hain.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous22 · Project #5 — CNN se person detection (Nicla Vision)→ Next24 · Project #6 — GAN se music generation (MAESTRO)
24Chapter 4 · Deep Learning

Project #6 — GAN se music generation (MAESTRO)

Project #6 me tum ek GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) se piano music generate karte ho. Ye book ka sabse creative project hai — aur sabse heavy bhi.

GAN ka idea: do networks ek dusre se ladte hain. Generator fake music banata hai, Discriminator pehchanne ki koshish karta hai ki music asli hai ya nakli. Dono improve hote jate hain — jab discriminator ki accuracy 50% par aa jaye (matlab wo guess kar raha hai), to generator jeet gaya.

Dataset — MAESTRO: lagbhag 200 hours piano performance, 1,280 files, 80.64 MB, 1,276 MIDI files. Har file me note timings aur velocities hain.

Generator architecture: 1000-dim noise input → Dense 256/512/1024 (LeakyReLU + batch norm) → tanh output (100 notes). Noise se shuru karke, dheere-dheere music banta hai.

Discriminator architecture: LSTM 512 + BiLSTM 512 + Dense 512/256/100 + sigmoid. Sequence ko aage-peeche padhkar decide karta hai: asli ya nakli.

Training details: 50% dropout (overfitting rokne ke liye), early stopping patience 20 (20 epochs tak improvement na ho to ruk jao). Training desktop par hoti hai — device par nahi.

Deploy (Ch 11 me): trained generator ko quantize karke Pico par chalaya jata hai — Project #20. Music generation embedded par chal sakta hai, yehi is project ka proof hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 4 — Deep Learning
← Previous23 · RNN, LSTM aur BRNN — sequence models→ Next25 · EDA workflow — data ko samajhna
25Chapter 5 · Exploratory Data Analysis

EDA workflow — data ko samajhna

EDA (Exploratory Data Analysis) ka matlab hai — model banane se pehle data ko achhe se samajhna. Book kehta hai ki jo log seedha model train karne lagte hain, wo data ki problems ko model me daal dete hain.

EDA workflow ke steps:

  • 1. Data dekho: kitne rows, kitne columns, kis type ka data? Missing values kitni hain?
  • 2. Descriptive statistics: mean, median, standard deviation, min, max. Har column ke liye.
  • 3. Distributions dekho: data normal hai ya skewed? Skewness aur kurtosis se pata chalta hai.
  • 4. Outliers dhoondho: IQR, z-score, Isolation Forest, DBSCAN — kaunsa tareeka kitne outliers batata hai?
  • 5. Correlations dekho: kaunsa feature target se judta hai? Correlation matrix aur mutual information se.
  • 6. Time patterns dekho: time-series data me trend, seasonality, aur regime changes.

Skewness aur kurtosis: skewness batata hai distribution kitna tedha hai (0 = symmetric, negative = left-skewed). Kurtosis batata hai tails kitne heavy hain. Project #7 me current ka skewness –1.422 aur kurtosis 7.025 tha — matlab data bilkul normal nahi hai.

EDA ka golden rule: data ko plot kiye bina model mat banao. Ek plot hazaar statistics se zyada batata hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 5 — Exploratory Data Analysis
← Previous24 · Project #6 — GAN se music generation (MAESTRO)→ Next26 · Project #7 — Battery SOC par EDA
26Chapter 5 · Exploratory Data Analysis

Project #7 — Battery SOC par EDA

Project #7 me tum Ch 3 wale LG 18650HG2 dataset par poori EDA karte ho — wahi 669,956 rows. Ye project dikhata hai ki EDA se kya-kya pata chalta hai, jo seedha model banane se kabhi pata nahi chalta.

Temperature bands: dataset chaar hisson me bata hai — index 0: 1–184,257 @ 0°C; index 10: 184,258–337,973 @ 10°C; index 25: 337,974–510,530 @ 25°C; index N10: 510,531–669,956 @ –10°C. Har band ka behavior alag hai.

Outlier detection — har method alag count deta hai:

MethodOutliers mile
Benchmark (IQR-based)2,639
Z-score2,473
IQR1,201
Isolation Forest (1%)2,565
Isolation Forest (10%)2,107
DBSCAN2,639 (0% — kuch nahi mila)
Domain-specific367 (86% — sabse relevant)
Hybrid344 (87%)

Lesson: outlier ka koi ek "sahi" jawab nahi hai. Domain knowledge (battery physics) se jo outliers mile (367), wo statistical methods se mile hazaaron se zyada useful the. Data ko samajhne ke liye domain samajhna zaroori hai.

Correlations (SOC ke saath): average voltage 0.9688, voltage 0.9348, voltage–avg voltage 0.9766. Matlab voltage SOC ka best predictor hai — yehi Project #2 ke lookup table ki buniyad thi.

Mutual information: average voltage 1.9595, voltage 1.8195, average current 1.2613, current 1.2157, temperature 0.7942. Temperature ka score sabse kam — SOC predict karne me temperature ka seedha role kam hai.

Resampling: 669,956 rows ko plot karne ke liye har 100th point liya gaya — warna plot hi nahi banta. EDA me sampling ek practical skill hai.

← Previous25 · EDA workflow — data ko samajhna→ Next27 · Smart sensor kya hai — Moravec's paradox
27Chapter 6 · Smart Sensors

Smart sensor kya hai — Moravec's paradox

Smart sensor sirf sense nahi karta — wo sochta bhi hai. Ek normal sensor raw data deta hai (jaise temperature = 24.5°C). Ek smart sensor data ko process karke decision deta hai (jaise "room garam ho raha hai, AC on karo").

Moravec's paradox: jo kaam insaan ko mushkil lagta hai (jaise chess, maths), wo computer ko aasan lagta hai. Aur jo kaam insaan ko aasan lagta hai (jaise chalna, dekhna, chhuna), wo computer ko bahut mushkil lagta hai. Isiliye robot ko chalna sikhana, chess khelna sikhane se zyada mushkil hai.

Iska embedded AI se kya lena: perception (dekhna, sunna, mehsoos karna) hi sabse mushkil kaam hai. Isliye sensors aur unka data — yehi embedded AI ki buniyad hai. Model to baad me aata hai; pehle sensor sahi hona chahiye.

Smart sensor ki pehchan:

  • Onboard processing: sensor ke andar hi MCU ya ML core (jaise ISM330BX me FSM aur MLC).
  • Digital output: raw analog ki jagah processed digital data — jaise "portrait up" ya "landscape left".
  • Self-calibration: sensor khud apni drift ko correct karta hai.
  • Event-driven: sirf tab data bhejta hai jab kuch badle — battery bachti hai.

Example: ISM330BX IMU ke andar finite state machine hai — wo khud detect karta hai ki device portrait hai ya landscape, bina MCU ko pareshan kiye. MCU tabhi jaagta hai jab orientation badle.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 6 — Smart Sensors
← Previous26 · Project #7 — Battery SOC par EDA→ Next28 · Adaptive sensing — 3-layer architecture
28Chapter 6 · Smart Sensors

Adaptive sensing — 3-layer architecture

Adaptive sensing ka matlab hai — sensor apni sampling ko situation ke hisaab se badle. Jab kuch nahi ho raha, to dheere sample karo (battery bachao). Jab kuch important ho raha hai, to tez sample karo (data mat chhodo).

3-layer architecture:

  • Layer 1 — Sense: sensor data collect karta hai. Low-power mode me slow sampling.
  • Layer 2 — Decide: onboard logic decide karta hai ki data important hai ya nahi. Threshold cross hua? Pattern badla?
  • Layer 3 — Adapt: sampling rate, resolution ya sensor mode ko badlo. Important event par full speed, boring time par sleep.

Example — activity tracking: jab user so raha hai, accelerometer 10 Hz par sample karta hai. Jab user daudne lage, to 100 Hz par. Battery 10x zyada chalti hai, aur data bhi poora milta hai.

Energy ka hisaab: sensor ko har sample par energy lagti hai — ADC, processing, transmission. Sampling rate aadhi karo, to energy lagbhag aadhi. Isliye adaptive sensing battery-powered devices me sabse bada energy saver hai.

Trade-off: adaptive sensing me risk hai — agar decide karne wala logic galat ho, to important event miss ho sakta hai. Isliye threshold aur hysteresis ko carefully tune karna padta hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 6 — Smart Sensors
← Previous27 · Smart sensor kya hai — Moravec's paradox→ Next29 · Project #8 — Compressed sensing (DHT11)
29Chapter 6 · Smart Sensors

Project #8 — Compressed sensing (DHT11)

Project #8 me tum compressed sensing se DHT11 temperature sensor ko kam sample karke bhi poora signal recover karte ho. Idea: agar signal sparse hai (matlab usme kam information hai), to kam samples se bhi use dobara banaya ja sakta hai.

Setup: DHT11 se 100 readings, har 10 minute par. Phir sirf 20 random samples lo — matlab 80% data phenk do. Kya bache hue 20 se poora signal recover ho sakta hai?

FFT sparsity: temperature signal ko frequency domain me dekho (FFT), to pata chalta hai ki zyada energy sirf kuch frequencies par hai — signal sparse hai. Isi liye compressed sensing kaam karta hai.

Stationarity check: ADF test ka p-value lagbhag 0.24 — matlab signal non-stationary hai (uske statistics samay ke saath badalte hain). Ye compressed sensing ko mushkil banata hai.

Results — interpolation methods ki tulna:

MethodMSERMSEMAEPSNR
Linear interpolation0.090.31570.147937.62
Staircase (hold)0.150.38730.1535.84

Lesson: linear interpolation staircase se behtar hai — MSE 0.09 vs 0.15. Aur 20% samples se bhi signal kaafi had tak recover ho jata hai. Battery-powered sensor ke liye ye bahut badi jeet hai: 5x kam sampling = 5x zyada battery life.

30Chapter 6 · Smart Sensors

Project #9 — FSM se orientation detection (ISM330BX)

Project #9 me tum ISM330BX IMU ke andar ki finite state machine (FSM) ko program karke device ki orientation detect karte ho — bina MCU ko jagaye.

Hardware: ISM330BX IMU, MKI245KA + MKI109V3 adapter boards par, STM32F401VE microcontroller ke saath. ODR (output data rate) 30 Hz.

FSM kya hai: ek state machine jo sensor ke andar chalti hai. States hain: portrait up, portrait down, landscape left, landscape right. Accelerometer data se state badalta hai.

Threshold: 0.8g — jab kisi axis par acceleration 0.8g se zyada ho, to orientation us taraf hai. Float16 me 0.8g = 0x3A66.

Timer: TIMER3 0x0F = 15 samples ≈ 500 ms — orientation tabhi badle jab 500 ms tak wahi rahe. Isse jhatke se galat detection nahi hota.

Output codes (OUTS register):

CodeOrientation
0x10Portrait up (–y ≥ 0.8g)
0x20Portrait down
0x04Landscape left
0x08Landscape right

Poori FSM: sirf 7 statements aur 4 variables — itni chhoti hai ki sensor ke andar chal jati hai. MCU ko sirf tab interrupt milta hai jab orientation badle.

Lesson: sensor ke andar compute karna sabse efficient hai. MCU soya rehta hai, battery bachti hai, aur response bhi tez milta hai.

31Chapter 7 · IMU Data Preprocessing

Frames — body, LTP, NED, ENU

IMU se orientation nikalne se pehle ye samajhna zaroori hai ki "upar" ka matlab kya hai — kyunki sensor aur duniya ke "upar" alag hote hain. Isi liye coordinate frames hote hain.

Body frame: device ke saath juda hua frame. X aage, Y side, Z upar (device ke hisaab se). Device ghume to body frame bhi ghumta hai.

LTP (Local Tangent Plane): zameen se juda frame. Device kahan hai, us jagah ka tangent plane. Isme gravity hamesha neeche ki taraf hoti hai.

NED (North-East-Down): X = North, Y = East, Z = Down (zameen ki taraf). Aircraft aur navigation me standard hai.

ENU (East-North-Up): X = East, Y = North, Z = Up (aasman ki taraf). Maps aur GPS me common hai.

Kyun zaroori hai: accelerometer gravity ko body frame me measure karta hai. Tumhe orientation chahiye LTP frame me. In do frames ke beech ka rotation hi orientation hai — roll, pitch, yaw.

Roll, pitch, yaw: roll = X-axis ke aas-paas ghumav, pitch = Y-axis ke aas-paas, yaw = Z-axis ke aas-paas. Teen angles se poori orientation define hoti hai (Euler angles).

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 7 — IMU Data Preprocessing
← Previous30 · Project #9 — FSM se orientation detection (ISM330BX)→ Next32 · Tilt formulas — roll aur pitch kaise nikalein
32Chapter 7 · IMU Data Preprocessing

Tilt formulas — roll aur pitch kaise nikalein

Accelerometer se tilt nikalna IMU preprocessing ka pehla kadam hai. Idea simple hai: gravity hamesha neeche ki taraf hoti hai, to accelerometer ke readings se pata chalta hai ki device kitna tedha hai.

Basic physics: agar device ek axis par angle α se tedha hai, to us axis par acceleration:

Ax = g · sin α

jahan g = 9.81 m/s². Isse ulta karke angle nikal sakte ho: α = arcsin(Ax/g).

Teen formulas (accuracy badhti hai):

  • Single-axis: sirf ek axis use karo. Simple, lekin sirf ek direction me sahi. Roll ke liye Ax, pitch ke liye Ay.
  • Two-axis: do axes ka ratio lo — atan2 use karo. Zyada stable, kyunki g ka magnitude matter nahi karta.
  • Three-axis: teeno axes use karo, normalization ke saath. Sabse accurate, lekin compute zyada.

atan2 kyun: atan2(y, x) sahi quadrant batata hai — plain atan se angle ka sign aur quadrant galat ho sakta hai. Tilt formulas me hamesha atan2 use karo.

Magnetometer aur yaw: accelerometer se yaw nahi nikalta (gravity yaw me nahi badalti). Yaw ke liye magnetometer chahiye — Earth ke magnetic field se North dhoondho, phir tilt-compensation lagao.

Declination: magnetic North aur true North me fark hota hai. Book ke location par declination 12.717° (12°43′) thi. Apne location ki declination check karo — bina iske compass galat dikhayega.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 7 — IMU Data Preprocessing
← Previous31 · Frames — body, LTP, NED, ENU→ Next33 · Project #10 — Angle formulas ka test
33Chapter 7 · IMU Data Preprocessing

Project #10 — Angle formulas ka test

Project #10 me tum teeno tilt formulas ko Nano 33 BLE (LSM9DS1 IMU) par test karte ho aur dekhte ho ki kaunsa formula kitna accurate hai.

Table 7-3 — RMSE (degrees, kam = behtar):

FormulaRoll RMSEPitch RMSE
Single-axis0.29100.8947
Two-axis0.38121.5874
Three-axis0.28040.9145

Table 7-4 — Bias (degrees): roll ka bias lagbhag –0.1° se –0.2°, pitch ka 0.5° se 0.78°. Bias matlab systematic error — har reading me wahi galti. Bias ko calibrate karke hata sakte ho.

Surprise: two-axis formula single-axis se kharab nikla (pitch RMSE 1.5874 vs 0.8947). Theory me two-axis behtar hona chahiye tha. Asli wajah: sensor noise aur calibration errors. Isi liye measure karo, assume mat karo.

Three-axis sabse accha: roll RMSE 0.2804 — sabse kam. Lekin compute bhi sabse zyada. Embedded me trade-off: accuracy vs compute.

Practical tip: formulas ko static test (device khada hai) par test karo, phir dynamic test (device hil raha hai) par. Static me accelerometer accha hai; dynamic me gyroscope ki zaroorat padti hai — Ch 8 me fusion aata hai.

34Chapter 7 · IMU Data Preprocessing

Gyro drift, magnetometer aur dead reckoning

Accelerometer sirf static tilt batata hai. Jab device hil raha ho, to gyroscope chahiye — lekin gyroscope ki apni problems hain.

Gyro drift: gyroscope angular velocity measure karta hai. Angle nikalne ke liye integrate karna padta hai — aur integration se chhoti galtiyan bhi jama ho jati hain. Book me stationary device par drift lagbhag 1° per 10 seconds thi. Matlab 10 minute me 60° ki galti — bina correction ke gyro akele kaam nahi karta.

Integration — Riemann sum: angle = purana angle + (angular velocity × time step). Time step chhota ho to accuracy behtar, lekin compute zyada.

Magnetometer: Earth ke magnetic field se yaw milta hai. Lekin do problems hain: hard iron (permanent magnetic interference — jaise paas me magnet) aur soft iron (magnetic field ko distort karne wali cheezein — jaise metal). Dono ko calibrate karke hatana padta hai.

Tilt-compensated yaw: magnetometer ko tilt ke hisaab se correct karo — warna device tedha ho to compass galat dikhayega.

Dead reckoning: bina GPS ke position estimate karna — acceleration ko do baar integrate karke. Lekin galti tezi se badhti hai: 0.01 m/s² bias se 10 second me 0.5 meter ki galti. Isliye dead reckoning sirf chhote samay ke liye kaam karta hai — phir GPS ya koi aur reference chahiye.

Summary: accelerometer = static me accha, dynamic me kharab. Gyroscope = dynamic me accha, drift karta hai. Magnetometer = yaw deta hai, interference se pareshan. Teeno ko milana padta hai — Ch 8 me sensor fusion.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 7 — IMU Data Preprocessing
← Previous33 · Project #10 — Angle formulas ka test→ Next35 · Sensor fusion aur complementary filter
35Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Sensor fusion aur complementary filter

Sensor fusion ka matlab hai — kai sensors ka data milakar ek behtar estimate banana. Ek sensor akele kabhi kaafi nahi hota: accelerometer static me accha hai, gyroscope dynamic me. Dono ko milao, to dono ke fayde milte hain.

Complementary filter — sabse simple fusion:

angle = α × (purana angle + gyro × dt) + (1 – α) × accel_angle

α (alpha) ek weight hai, 0 se 1 ke beech. α zyada ho to gyro par zyada bharosa; kam ho to accelerometer par.

Time constant τ se α nikalna: α = τ / (τ + Δt). Book me τ = 0.75 s, Δt = 0.0067 s → α ≈ 0.99. Matlab gyro par 99% bharosa, accelerometer sirf drift correct karne ke liye.

Project #11 me α = 0.95 (τ = 0.4 s, 50 Hz sampling). α chunna ek tuning ka kaam hai — zyada α se response tez lekin drift zyada; kam α se drift kam lekin response slow.

Complementary filter kyun accha hai: sirf kuch lines ka code, koi matrix maths nahi, microcontroller par microseconds me chalta hai. Bahut se projects me yehi kaafi hai — Kalman filter ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Kab Kalman chahiye: jab noise ka model pata ho aur best possible estimate chahiye — to Kalman/EKF. Lekin uski keemat hai: zyada code, zyada compute, zyada tuning.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion
← Previous34 · Gyro drift, magnetometer aur dead reckoning→ Next36 · Quaternions aur gimbal lock
36Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Quaternions aur gimbal lock

Euler angles (roll, pitch, yaw) samajhne me aasan hain, lekin unme ek badi problem hai — gimbal lock.

Gimbal lock kya hai: jab pitch ±90° par pahunchta hai, to roll aur yaw ek hi axis par aa jate hain — ek degree of freedom kho jata hai. System confuse ho jata hai ki kaunsa angle badla.

Apollo 11 ka kissa: Moon mission me gimbal lock ke kareeb pahunch gaye the — astronaut ko manual maneuver se bachna pada. Yehi wajah hai ki aaj ke systems quaternions use karte hain.

Quaternions: chaar numbers (w, x, y, z) se orientation represent karo. Euler angles ki tarah intuitive nahi, lekin:

  • Koi gimbal lock nahi: chaaro numbers hamesha valid rehte hain.
  • Interpolation smooth hai: do orientations ke beech smooth transition (slerp).
  • Compute efficient hai: rotation matrix se kam operations.

Euler vs Tait-Bryan: dono angle conventions hain — farak sirf itna hai ki axes kis order me rotate hote hain. Code me convention saaf likhna zaroori hai, warna do systems ki orientation match nahi karegi.

Practical advice: internal calculations me quaternion use karo, display aur debugging ke liye Euler angles me convert karo. User ko quaternion mat dikhao — wo samajh nahi payega.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion
← Previous35 · Sensor fusion aur complementary filter→ Next37 · Madgwick aur Mahony filters
37Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Madgwick aur Mahony filters

Complementary filter ke baad agle level ke do filters hain — Madgwick aur Mahony. Dono quaternion-based hain, aur dono embedded me bahut popular hain.

Madgwick filter: gradient descent se orientation estimate karta hai. Accelerometer aur magnetometer ka data use karke gyro drift ko correct karta hai.

  • β (beta) = 0.041 steady state me — ye filter ka gain hai. Beta zyada ho to response tez, kam ho to stable.
  • Initialization me β = 10 — shuru me tezi se converge karne ke liye, phir 0.041 par le aao.
  • ζ (zeta) = 0 / 0.015 — gyro bias estimation ke liye. Zeta se filter gyro ka bias bhi seekhta hai.
  • Accuracy: <0.8° RMS — bahut accha, embedded ke liye kaafi.

Mahony filter: complementary filter ka quaternion version — PI controller se drift correct karta hai.

  • Kp = 10 (is project me), Ki = 0. Original 2008 paper me Kp = 0.04 tha — farak isliye kyunki sampling rate aur application alag hai.
  • Kp proportional gain hai — galti ko kitni tezi se correct karo. Ki integral gain hai — steady bias ko khatm karo.

Kaunsa chunna hai: Madgwick jab magnetometer bhi hai aur best accuracy chahiye; Mahony jab code simple rakhna hai aur sirf accelerometer + gyro kaafi hai. Dono hi complementary filter se behtar hain.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion
← Previous36 · Quaternions aur gimbal lock→ Next38 · Kalman filter aur EKF
38Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Kalman filter aur EKF

Kalman filter sensor fusion ka gold standard hai. Ye sirf sensors ko average nahi karta — wo har sensor ki uncertainty ko samajhta hai aur mathematically best estimate nikalta hai.

Kalman filter ke do steps (baar-baar):

  • Predict: model se andaza lagao — agle step me state kya hoga? (Gyro se angle predict karo.)
  • Update: measurement se correct karo — sensor ne kya bataya? (Accelerometer se correct karo.)

Kalman gain: predict aur measurement me se kisko kitna bharosa dena hai, ye Kalman gain decide karta hai. Gain apne aap adjust hota hai — jab measurement reliable ho, to gain zyada; jab model reliable ho, to gain kam.

EKF (Extended Kalman Filter): Kalman filter sirf linear systems ke liye hai. Orientation nonlinear hai, isliye EKF use hota hai — nonlinear ko har step par linearize karke.

Book ka EKF setup: state = roll + pitch, initial covariance 0.01. Covariance batati hai estimate par kitna bharosa hai — shuru me kam bharosa, phir badhta hai.

Kalman vs complementary:

AspectComplementaryKalman / EKF
Code~10 lines~200 lines + matrix maths
TuningEk parameter (α)Kai matrices (Q, R, P)
AccuracyAcchiBest possible
ComputeMicrosecondsMilliseconds

Rule of thumb: pehle complementary try karo. Agar accuracy kaafi nahi hai, tab Kalman par jao.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion
← Previous37 · Madgwick aur Mahony filters→ Next39 · Project #11 — Complementary filter (α = 0.95)
39Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Project #11 — Complementary filter (α = 0.95)

Project #11 me tum Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev 2 par complementary filter implement karke orientation estimate karte ho.

Setup: α = 0.95, time constant τ = 0.4 s, sampling rate 50 Hz. Matlab har 20 ms par ek naya estimate.

Formula (code me):

// angle = alpha * (angle + gyro * dt) + (1 - alpha) * accel_angle
roll  = 0.95 * (roll  + gyroX * dt) + 0.05 * accelRoll;
pitch = 0.95 * (pitch + gyroY * dt) + 0.05 * accelPitch;

Kya hota hai: gyro se angle tezi se update hota hai (95% weight), accelerometer se dheere-dheere drift correct hota hai (5% weight). Result: smooth aur stable orientation.

Test: device ko ghumao aur dekho — estimate bina lag ke follow karta hai, aur rukne par drift nahi karta. Agar α = 1 kar do (sirf gyro), to drift dikhega. Agar α = 0 kar do (sirf accelerometer), to hilne par noise dikhega.

α ko tune karna: device ko static rakho aur drift dekho — α kam karo. Device ko tez ghumao aur lag dekho — α badhao. Sahi α wahi hai jahan dono acceptable hon.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion

Project #12 — Filter comparison (Table 8-4)

Project #12 me tum saare filters ko ek hi data par chala kar tulna karte ho — Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev 1 par. Kaunsa filter kab jeet ta hai, yehi is project ka jawab hai.

Table 8-4 — filter comparison (summary):

FilterResult
No filter (raw)Catastrophic — roll mean 274.1, pitch mean 5381.6 (drift se angle hazaaron degree!)
ComplementaryAccha — simple aur stable
MadgwickAccha — best overall balance
MahonySabse consistent — har test me stable
EKFBest yaw — lekin compute sabse zyada

Key findings:

  • Bina filter ke kuch nahi chalta: raw integration se angle hazaaron degree drift kar jata hai. Filter zaroori hai, optional nahi.
  • Mahony sabse consistent: har test me stable result — isliye bahut se projects me Mahony default choice hai.
  • EKF ka yaw best hai: magnetometer ko sabse acche se use karta hai. Lekin code aur compute ki keemat hai.
  • Madgwick best balance: accuracy aur simplicity ke beech.

Interview tip: "Kaunsa sensor fusion filter use karoge?" ka jawab hamesha "it depends" se shuru hota hai — phir constraints batao: compute, accuracy, yaw chahiye ya nahi, magnetometer hai ya nahi.

Project #13 — IMUs ki static angle accuracy

Project #13 me tum teen alag IMUs ki static angle accuracy measure karte ho — Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev 1 par. Kaunsa IMU kitna accurate hai, yehi sawal hai.

Test: device ko static (bina hile) rakho aur gravity vector ka magnitude measure karo. Ideal value 1.0g hai — jitna kareeb, utna accha.

Results:

IMUMean norm (g)SDError
BMI2700.99700.00150.0304
LSM9DS10.98820.00120.0234
MPU60501.04640.00530.0506

Interpretation: LSM9DS1 ka error sabse kam (0.0234) — static accuracy me best. BMI270 bhi accha (0.0304) aur uska standard deviation sabse kam (0.0015) — matlab consistent. MPU6050 sabse kharab (0.0506, SD 0.0053) — purana sensor hai, aaj ke naye sensors se peeche hai.

Lesson: sensor chunne se pehle datasheet ke numbers par bharosa mat karo — khud measure karo. Datasheet ideal conditions ke numbers deta hai; tumhara board, tumhara power supply aur tumhara environment alag hai.

Calibration ka role: har IMU me bias hota hai — use calibrate karke hatao, to accuracy aur badhti hai. Calibration ke bina best IMU bhi kharab result de sakta hai.

42Chapter 8 · Sensor Fusion

Project #14 — ISM330BX SFLP sensor fusion

Project #14 me tum ISM330BX IMU ke andar ke SFLP (Sensor Fusion Low Power) engine ko test karte ho — sensor khud fusion karta hai, MCU ko kuch nahi karna padta.

SFLP kya deta hai:

  • Game rotation vector: quaternion — device ki orientation, bina magnetometer ke.
  • Gravity vector: gravity kis direction me hai — tilt nikalne ke liye.
  • Gyro bias: sensor khud apna gyro bias estimate karta hai aur correct karta hai.

Result: SFLP ka RMSE lagbhag MPU6050 ka ek-chauthai hai. Matlab sensor ke andar ka fusion, MCU par chalne wale MPU6050 ke fusion se 4x behtar hai.

Kyun behtar hai: SFLP sensor ke liye specially design hua hai — uske noise characteristics, uski calibration, sab kuch onboard hai. MCU par generic filter itna tuned nahi ho sakta.

Lesson — sensor fusion ka future: fusion MCU se sensor ke andar ja raha hai. ISM330BX me FSM, MLC aur SFLP — teeno onboard hain. Aane wale samay me sensor sirf data nahi dega, decision bhi dega. Embedded engineer ko ye samajhna hoga ki sensor ke andar kya chal raha hai.

Trade-off: onboard fusion se control kam milta hai — tum filter ke parameters ko utna tune nahi kar sakte jitna apne code me kar sakte ho. Lekin power aur simplicity ka fayda zyada hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 8 — Sensor Fusion

43Chapter 9 · Sensor Machine Learning

Sensor data par ML — Kalman vs ML

Ch 8 me tumne classical sensor fusion seekha (Kalman, Madgwick). Ch 9 me sawal hai: jab ML ko sensor data par lagao, to kya hota hai?

Kalman vs ML (Figure 9-1 — impulse noise par): Kalman filter impulse noise (achanak bada spike) par kharab perform karta hai — kyunki wo assume karta hai ki noise Gaussian hai. ML model, agar use impulse noise wale examples se train kiya ho, to use handle kar leta hai. ML tab jeet ta hai jab noise ka pattern pata ho aur data se seekha ja sake.

Sensor ML ke liye model families:

  • Decision trees / Random forests: simple, interpretable, embedded par chal sakte hain. Project #15 me decision tree hi use hota hai.
  • SVM (Support Vector Machines): chhote dataset par accha, lekin deploy karna mushkil.
  • RNN / LSTM: time-series sensor data ke liye — sequence yaad rakhta hai.
  • CNN: spectrogram ya image-like sensor data ke liye.
  • Autoencoders: anomaly detection ke liye — normal data ko compress karke dobara banao; agar reconstruction error zyada ho, to anomaly hai.
  • KNN: simple, lekin memory heavy — poora dataset device par rakhna padta hai.

Sensor ML ki khaas challenges: data noisy hota hai, sampling irregular hoti hai, sensors drift karte hain, aur labels milna mushkil hai. Isliye sensor ML me feature engineering (Ch 7 ke formulas) aur EDA (Ch 5) bahut zaroori hai.

Rule: pehle classical approach try karo (Kalman, threshold). Agar wo fail ho, tab ML lao. ML ko pehla option mat banao.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 9 — Sensor Machine Learning
← Previous42 · Project #14 — ISM330BX SFLP sensor fusion→ Next44 · Project #15 — Robot arm fault detection (MLC)
44Chapter 9 · Sensor Machine Learning

Project #15 — Robot arm fault detection (MLC)

Project #15 me tum ek 6-DOF robot arm me fault detect karte ho — ISM330BX ke andar ke MLC (Machine Learning Core) se. Arm ke servos ko current aur motion data se pata chalta hai ki kuch gadbad hai ya nahi.

Hardware: 6-DOF arm, 6× MG996R servos (4.8V par 9.4 kg·cm torque, 6.0V par 11 kg·cm; speed 0.17 s/60° @ 4.8V; stall current 2.5 A @ 6V). Pololu Maestro servo controller: 4000 = 0°, 6000 = 90°, 8000 = 180° (0.25 µs units, 20 ms / 50 Hz). Power supply 5V 15A (6 × 2.3A = 13.8A peak).

Pick-and-place cycle: lagbhag 19 second. Anomaly: 20% chance — servo freeze ho jata hai (jaanboojh kar fault inject kiya jata hai).

MLC decision tree: 15 features (AFS — advanced feature selection se chune gaye), 4 leaves, 7 nodes. Itna chhota tree sensor ke andar chal jata hai.

Results: accuracy 95.43%, 591 instances (564 correct, 27 wrong), kappa 91.80%. Anomaly recall 1.00 (koi anomaly miss nahi), precision 0.80. Confusion: stationary 0, nominal 4, anomaly 8 (galat classify).

Registers: MLC1_SRC 0x70 se MLC4_SRC 0x73, MLC_STATUS 0x15. MCU ko sirf status register padhna hai — decision sensor ke andar hota hai.

Lesson: anomaly detection me recall (koi fault miss na ho) precision se zyada important hai — false alarm se kaam rukta hai, lekin miss hua fault machine tod deta hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 9 — Sensor Machine Learning

45Chapter 10 · Real-Time Audio Noise Suppression

RNNoise — GRU se noise suppression

RNNoise ek neural network hai jo real-time me audio se shor hatata hai. Tum bol rahe ho, peeche fan chal raha hai — RNNoise fan ki awaaz hata kar sirf tumhari awaaz rakhta hai. Ye Project #16–17 ka core hai.

Architecture: GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) — LSTM ka halka version. Input: 42 features — 22 Bark bands (human hearing ke hisaab se frequency bands) se nikale gaye. Model sirf 87k parameters ka hai — bahut chhota.

Bark bands kya hain: human ear frequency ko linear nahi, logarithmic sunta hai. Bark scale isi ko capture karta hai — 22 bands me poori hearing range. Isse model ko wohi features milte hain jo kaan ke liye important hain.

VAD (Voice Activity Detection): output 0 se 1 ke beech — 0 matlab sirf shor hai, 1 matlab awaaz hai. VAD se pata chalta hai kab bolna ho raha hai aur kab nahi.

Real-time constraint: audio frame hai 480 samples @ 16 kHz = 30 ms. Har frame ko 30 ms se kam me process karna hai, warna audio atak jayega. Isi liye benchmark important hai — Project #16 me Pico vs Pico 2.

RNNoise kyun khaas hai: ye classical noise suppression (spectral subtraction) se behtar hai, kyunki wo shor ke pattern ko seekhta hai, sirf average nahi karta.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 10 — Real-Time Audio Noise Suppression
← Previous44 · Project #15 — Robot arm fault detection (MLC)→ Next46 · Project #16 — Pico vs Pico 2 benchmark
46Chapter 10 · Real-Time Audio Noise Suppression

Project #16 — Pico vs Pico 2 benchmark

Project #16 me tum RNNoise ko Pico aur Pico 2 par chala kar benchmark karte ho — ek hi code, do chips, kitna fark?

Results — ek 480-sample frame process karne me time:

BoardTime per frameReal-time?
Pico (RP2040)386,429 µs = 0.39 sNahi — 30 ms frame ke liye 13x slow
Pico 2 (RP2350)22,883 µs = 0.02 sHaan — 30 ms ke andar

Pico 2 lagbhag 17x tez hai. Iska matlab: Pico par RNNoise real-time nahi chal sakta — audio atak jayega. Pico 2 par chal sakta hai — 22.9 ms me frame process ho jata hai, 30 ms ke budget ke andar.

Microphone — T3902 PDM mic:

ModeClockCurrentAOP
Standard1.0–3.3 MHz430 µA120 dB SPL
High Performance4.1–4.8 MHz650 µA126 dB SPL
Low Power400–800 kHz185 µA—
Sleep<200 kHz<20 µA—

PDM clock: 1.024 MHz (16 kHz × 64). EIN (Equivalent Input Noise) 30 dB SPL — mic kitna quiet hai, ye batata hai.

Lesson: model chunne se pehle chip ki taakat measure karo. Pico 2 ka upgrade sirf "naya" nahi hai — ye real-time ML ko possible banata hai.

47Chapter 10 · Real-Time Audio Noise Suppression

Project #17 — Real-time audio system (Pico 2)

Project #17 me tum Pico 2 par poora real-time noise suppression system banate ho — microphone se lekar USB audio tak.

Dual-core design: Pico 2 ke do cores ka kaam bata hai — Core 1: audio capture + RNN inference, Core 0: USB (TinyUSB) + display. Dono cores parallel chalte hain, isliye audio kabhi nahi rukta.

Display: DFR0664 2-inch LCD, 320×240, ST7789 driver. PIO software SPI se chalaya jata hai — clk_div 2.0, Mode 3, pins BL 17 / DC 18 / RES 19 / CS 20 / DIN 26 / CLK 27, pio1.

FFT: CMSIS-DSP library se 256-point FFT @ 16 kHz — har bin 62.5 Hz. Hann window, Q15 fixed-point maths. FFT_BINS_SKIP 5 (neeche ki bins ignore karo), FFT_MAG_MAX 2000.0.

RP2350 Erratum E9: GPIO 0–29 par ek hardware bug hai — floating pins lagbhag 2V par latak jate hain. Fix: pull-down resistor ≤ 8.2 kΩ lagao. Yehi embedded reality hai — datasheet ka errata section bhi padho.

TinyUSB starvation: agar Core 0 par tud_task() time par na chale, to USB atak jata hai. Book me ek bug tha — LED sirf 2 Hz par blink kar rahi thi, kyunki USB task starve ho raha tha. Fix: tasks ko sahi priority aur timing do.

Poora system: mic → PDM → Core 1 (RNNoise) → clean audio → USB → PC. Aur display par live spectrum dikhta hai. Yehi ek real product ka prototype hai.

48Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

AI MIDI synthesizer — toolchain aur quantization

Chapter 11 me tum ek poora AI MIDI synthesizer banate ho — Pico par chalne wala, jo AI se music generate karta hai aur use bajata bhi hai. Ye book ka sabse lamba chapter hai — 8 projects (18–25) ek hi system ke hisse hain.

System ke hisse: piano keyboard (capacitive keys) → Pico (AI model + MIDI) → VS1053 synth chip (sound) → speaker. USB se MIDI bhi bhej sakte ho.

PTQ (Post-Training Quantization): trained GAN generator (float32, 4.1 MB) ko int8 me convert karo → lagbhag 1 MB. Matlab ~4x chhota, aur Pico par chal sakta hai.

Quantization ke details: representative dataset — 100 samples, N(0,1) latent vectors. Batch size 1 fix karo (warna shape mismatch). Input: [1,1000] int8, scale 0.03334758, zero-point 1. Output: [1,100,1] int8, scale 0.0078125, zero-point 0.

Scale aur zero-point kya hain: int8 sirf –128 se 127 tak ja sakta hai. Float value ko int8 me map karne ke liye formula hai: int8 = round(float / scale) + zero_point. Scale batata hai har step kitna bada hai; zero-point batata hai 0.0 kahan hai.

TFLM deployment: model ko xxd -i se C array banao, alignas(16) se align karo, tensor arena 4 KB do (estimated 3,340 bytes), sirf 4 ops register karo. MicroPrintf se debug karo.

PIO: keyboard aur synth ke liye 2 PIO blocks × 4 state machines, 9 instructions. PIO se timing-critical kaam CPU ko pareshan kiye bina hota hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 11 — Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

49Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Projects #18–20 — Toolchain, quantization, GAN deployment

Projects #18–20 synthesizer ki neenv hain — pehle toolchain test karo, phir model ko chhota karo, phir use device par chalao.

Project #18 — Software toolchain testing: Pico par blink se shuru karo. Toolchain (compiler, SDK, upload) kaam kar raha hai ya nahi, ye pehle verify karo. Agar blink nahi chalta, to aage badhne ka koi fayda nahi.

Project #19 — Model quantization: Ch 4 ke GAN generator ko PTQ se int8 me convert karo. Details pichle section me hain — 4.1 MB se ~1 MB. Quantization ke baad accuracy check karo: kya music abhi bhi accha hai? Agar nahi, to representative dataset badhao ya quantization-aware training karo.

Project #20 — GAN deployment testing: quantized model ko Pico par chalao aur output check karo. Tensor arena 4 KB, 4 ops. Agar model crash karta hai, to pehle arena size check karo — zyadatar TFLM crashes arena chhota hone se hote hain.

Teeno projects ka lesson: deployment ek alag skill hai — training se alag. Model train karna aasan hai; use device par chalana mushkil. Har step ko alag se test karo: toolchain, phir quantization, phir deployment.

Common pitfalls: batch size mismatch (quantization me batch 1 fix karo), alignment issues (alignas(16) bhoolna), aur ops missing (OpResolver me saare ops register karo).

50Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Project #21 — Piano keyboard banana

Project #21 me tum Pico par ek capacitive-touch piano keyboard banate ho — 14 keys, bina kisi mechanical switch ke.

14 keys: 12 notes (ek octave) + Octave – aur Octave +. Octave keys se poora keyboard upar-neeche shift hota hai.

Self-capacitive sensing: har key ek capacitor hai — ungli lagne se capacitance badhti hai. Pico us change ko detect karta hai. Koi moving part nahi, koi switch nahi — sirf PCB par copper pads.

PIO: CLOCK_DIV 40 (3.125 MHz), 1 MΩ resistors, pins GP2–GP15, 3 state machines. PIO har key ko tezi se scan karta hai.

Kaise kaam karta hai: har key ko charge karo, phir discharge time measure karo. Ungli lagi ho to capacitance zyada, discharge slow. Threshold se decide karo: key dabai gayi ya nahi.

Debounce: capacitive keys me bhi bounce hota hai — ungli lagte hi signal hilta hai. Software debounce (kuch ms tak stable rahe to hi key press mano) zaroori hai.

Lesson: capacitive sensing se keyboard sasta aur reliable banta hai — lekin tuning chahiye: threshold, sensitivity aur debounce, teeno ko apne haath aur environment ke hisaab se set karo.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 11 — Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer
← Previous49 · Projects #18–20 — Toolchain, quantization, GAN deployment→ Next51 · Project #22 — VS1053 hardware synth
51Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Project #22 — VS1053 hardware synth

Project #22 me tum VS1053b chip se ek hardware MIDI synthesizer banate ho — Pico MIDI bhejta hai, VS1053 use awaaz me badalta hai.

VS1053b kya hai: ek dedicated audio decoder/synth chip. MIDI notes ko real instrument sounds me badalta hai — piano, guitar, drums, sab kuch.

Crystal: 12.288 MHz crystal, C9 = C10 = 33 pF, R10 = 1 MΩ. Crystal ki frequency se chip ki timing aur audio quality decide hoti hai.

Power: AP7312 dual LDO — 3.3V aur 1.8V dono deta hai. Soft-start: R11 100k + C14 100nF — power on hote waqt current spike rokne ke liye.

Real-time MIDI mode: GPIO0 low + GPIO1 high — chip ko MIDI mode me daalo. Normal mode me chip MP3 decode karta hai; MIDI mode me wo synth banta hai.

Optocoupler: 6N138-L — MIDI input ko electrically isolate karta hai. MIDI standard me isolation zaroori hai, taaki ground loops se noise na aaye.

Custom carrier PCB: VS1053 ko seedha breadboard par nahi laga sakte — isliye ek custom PCB banti hai. Yehi embedded hardware ka asli kaam hai: chip se lekar PCB tak.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 11 — Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

52Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Project #23 — Keyboard ko USB MIDI device banana

Project #23 me tum Pico ko ek USB MIDI device banate ho — computer ko lagega ki ek asli MIDI keyboard juda hai.

TinyUSB: Pico ke liye USB stack. USB MIDI class se Pico ek standard MIDI device ki tarah dikhta hai — koi driver install nahi karna padta, DAW (jaise Ableton, GarageBand) seedha pehchan leta hai.

USB descriptors: VID 0xCafe, product name "Pico USB MIDI". VID vendor ID hai — 0xCafe ek test VID hai, production me apna VID lena padta hai.

Bug — tud_task() starvation: book me ek bug aaya — LED sirf 2 Hz par blink kar rahi thi. Wajah: tud_task() ko time par call nahi ho raha tha, USB stack starve ho raha tha. Fix: main loop me tud_task() ko regularly call karo, aur heavy kaam ko uske aas-paas mat rakho.

MIDI messages: Note On (key dabai), Note Off (key chhodi), velocity (kitni zor se dabai). Har message 3 bytes ka hota hai — status, note number, velocity.

Test: Pico ko PC se jodo, DAW kholo, keyboard bajao — sound PC se aana chahiye. Agar nahi aaye, to pehle USB descriptors check karo, phir MIDI messages.

53Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Project #24 — pico-ai (AI music generation)

Project #24 me tum quantized GAN model ko Pico par chala kar AI se music generate karte ho — yehi pico-ai hai.

OCTAVE – key ka naya kaam: OCTAVE – button ko AI Generate ke roop me repurpose kiya gaya hai. Button dabao, AI 100 notes generate karta hai. Octave + abhi bhi octave shift karta hai — 4 octaves tak capped hai.

Seed mapping: user jo note bajata hai, use seed banaya jata hai — formula: (midi – 48) / 2 + zero-point. Matlab tumhari input se AI ki output influence hoti hai.

Output: 100-note sequence — model se aata hai, phir MIDI notes me convert hota hai, phir VS1053 synth par bajta hai.

Flow: key press → seed → GAN inference (Pico par, int8) → 100 notes → MIDI → synth → sound. Poora loop device par chalta hai — cloud ki zaroorat nahi.

Latency: inference itna tez hai ki button dabate hi music shuru ho jata hai. Yehi embedded AI ka magic hai — AI ko instrument bana dena.

Lesson: AI music generation sirf research nahi hai — ye ek bajane layak instrument ban sakta hai, jo battery par chalta hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 11 — Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

54Chapter 11 · Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

Project #25 — Procedural composition

Project #25 me tum AI ke bina music generate karte ho — procedural composition se. Do tareeke: arpeggiator aur Markov chain. Dono deterministic hain, lekin sunne me musical lagte hain.

Arpeggiator: ek chord ke notes ko ek-ek karke bajao. Book me C7 chord, 40 notes, 10 cycles, 286 ms interval, lagbhag 11 second. Arpeggio se simple chord bhi interesting lagta hai.

Markov chain: agla note pichle note par depend karta hai — ek 12×12 transition matrix. Har row batati hai ki is note ke baad kaunsa note aane ki kitni probability hai. Matrix ko training data (ya music theory) se bharo.

Details: MIDI 60 = C4 (middle C) root note. Buffer: 32 notes. Chain chalao, notes generate karo, bajao.

AI vs procedural: GAN creative lekin unpredictable hai — kabhi bekar notes bhi deta hai. Markov predictable hai — hamesha musical, lekin kabhi surprising nahi. Dono ko milakar best result milta hai: Markov se structure, GAN se variation.

Lesson: har cheez ke liye ML ki zaroorat nahi hai. Kabhi-kabhi ek simple algorithm (Markov chain) ML se behtar result deta hai — aur 100x kam compute me.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 11 — Build an AI MIDI Synthesizer

55Chapter 12 · Build a Hot Word Detection Engine

Voice assistant flow — hot-word pipeline

Hot-word detection ka matlab hai — device hamesha sunta rahe, lekin tabhi jaage jab tum uska naam pukaro. "Hey" + device name bolte hi wo jaag jata hai. Ye Chapter 12 ka core hai.

Voice assistant flow (Figure 12-1): microphone → feature extraction → inference → threshold → wake → baaki pipeline (speech recognition, NLU, action). Hot-word sirf pehla gate hai — baaki kaam uske baad shuru hota hai.

Hot-word pipeline ke steps:

  • Feature extraction: audio ko spectrogram ya MFE features me badlo.
  • Inference: neural network features ko dekhkar decide kare — wake word hai ya nahi?
  • Threshold: confidence threshold se upar ho to hi wake karo — warna false alarm.

Multi-syllable wake words: "Hello World" jaise 2+ syllable wale words behtar hain — single syllable (jaise "Hey") par false alarm zyada hota hai. Lamba word = kam confusion.

MFE vs Syntiant log-Mel frontend: MFE (Mel-filterbank energy) standard feature extraction hai. Syntiant ka log-Mel frontend NDP120 chip ke liye optimize hai — wahi features jo chip ke neural engine ko chahiye.

Metrics: precision (kitne detections sahi the), recall (kitne real wake words pakde), F1 (dono ka balance), AUC, confusion matrix, FAR (false acceptance rate) aur FRR (false rejection rate). In sab ko Ch 12 me detail me samjhaya gaya hai.

SOURCESource: Embedded AI, No Starch Press, Chapter 12 — Build a Hot Word Detection Engine

Project #26 — Nicla Voice aur Alexa demo

Project #26 me tum Arduino Nicla Voice ko validate karte ho — pehle ek ready-made Alexa demo se, phir apne model ke liye taiyaar hote ho.

Nicla Voice hardware: nRF52832 microcontroller + Syntiant NDP120 neural decision processor. Board sirf 22.86 mm square hai — chhota, lekin <1 mW me hamesha-on listening karta hai.

NDP120 firmware update — 3 files:

FileSizeKaam
mcu_fw_120_v91.synpkg22,636 bytesMCU firmware
dsp_firmware_v91.synpkg79,828 bytesDSP firmware
alexa_334_NDP120_B0_v11_v91.synpkg417,828 bytes (3265 blocks)Alexa model

Uploader commands (YModem): L = list files, S = send, F = format, R = reset, Y = yes. Firmware update ke liye syntiant-uploader-osx send -m "Y" -w "Y" -p /dev/cu.usbmodemA02D31B03 <file>.synpkg jaisi command chalti hai.

Test: AlexaDemo sketch flash karo (File → Examples → NDP → AlexaDemo), Serial Monitor kholo. "Alexa" bolne par detection dikhna chahiye (Figure 12-3 jaisa output).

Lesson: apna model train karne se pehle hardware ko ready-made model se validate karo. Agar Alexa demo nahi chalta, to problem hardware ya firmware me hai — tumhare model me nahi.
